newsitem.title: SUDAN: 23 Congolese refugees starve to death in Sudan.
newsitem.headline: 23 Congolese refugees starve to death in Sudan.

text.p: Twenty-three people who fled the recent fighting in the Democratic Republic of the Congo have starved to death in south Sudan, the official Sudan News Agency (SUNA) reported on Monday.
Thousands of refugees feld Congo, formerly known as Zaire, in May after rebel leader Laurent Kabila ousted former president Mobutu Sese Seko.

SUNA said it did not know the exact number of refugees living in Sudan but added that there were 4,000 Congolese refugees in both the southern town of Juba and the capital Khartoum before the fighting.
Food is scarce in Sudan's south where the rebel Sudan People's Liberation Army has been fighting the government for almost 14 years.
Travellers to Juba, a strategic town which has often been the target of clashes between the state and rebels, say there is a food shortage and that some residents eat four meals a week.

But Assam Kabashi, the commissioner for refugees in Southern Sudan's Equatoria region, was quoted by SUNA as saying the conditions of the refugees had improved after intervention by the U.N. World Food Programme (WFP), the regional government and the military leaders in Juba.
SUNA said that a month's supply of food had also been sent to Juba.
